practical.title: INTENSIVE Lab — Implement & Compare Bubble / Selection / Insertion Sort (C)
practical.summary: Implement three classic in-place O(n^2) sorts in one C program, run them on separate copies of the same array, trace their step-by-step behavior (optional), and compare counts for comparisons and swaps to gain intuition about practical performance.

coachingPrompts: What do you predict will happen before you run it?
What evidence shows that your change worked?
Can you explain the result in your own words?

files.description: Runnable C starter file for the practical.

tasks.title: Scene 1 — Observe & Understand (Run the baseline)
tasks.narratorGuide: Hello — let's observe a baseline run. We'll compile and run the provided C program without edits. It prints the original array, runs Bubble, Selection, and Insertion on separate copies, and prints both the sorted results and counts of comparisons and swaps for each algorithm. Watching these numeric counts helps you move from abstract Big-O language to concrete work performed on this small input. Next we'll modify the input and then enable trace mode to step through operations.

tasks.title: Scene 2 — Modify & Experiment (Change input; see cause-and-effect)
tasks.narratorGuide: Great — next, change the input to a nearly-sorted case or use the provided 'sorted' preset. You only need a small edit (or pass an argument) to flip scenarios: nearly-sorted arrays favor Insertion Sort's O(n) best case. Run the program with the 'sorted' preset (./sort_demo sorted) to see counts drop for Insertion (and Bubble with the early-exit optimization) while Selection's comparisons remain the same. Observe and note why Selection doesn't improve.

tasks.title: Scene 3 — Build & Integrate (Enable tracing; step through operations)
tasks.narratorGuide: Excellent — now let's step through the algorithms. Re-run the program with the 'trace' flag (./sort_demo trace) to see line-by-line messages describing each compare and swap. Watch how Bubble repeatedly compares neighbors, Selection scans for a min and performs occasional swaps, and Insertion shifts elements into place. Use this trace to predict the next few operations before they appear; that active prediction is a powerful learning technique.

tasks.title: Scene 4 — Verify & Extend (Edge cases and final reflection)
tasks.narratorGuide: You're almost done — run reverse and duplicate presets to verify worst- and duplicate-handling behavior. For reverse-sorted data you'll see the greatest work (many swaps and comparisons) for Bubble and Insertion, while Selection's comparisons remain constant. For duplicates, notice that Bubble and Insertion remain stable (relative order preserved), while Selection might not. As an extension, try modifying the program to sort doubles or strings — that will require changing the array type and comparator logic.

safety.learnerWarning: This practical runs in an isolated workspace. Do not use real credentials or production resources.

cleanup.instructions: Discard the isolated workspace after completion.
